newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Balongan residue tanks full, crude unit shut again.
newsitem.headline: Balongan residue tanks full, crude unit shut again.

text.p: Indonesia's state-oil company Pertamina temporarily restarted its 125,000 barrels-per-day (bpd) crude distillation unit (CDU) at Balongan refinery over the weekend, but shut it down again on Monday because residue fuel tanks were full, Pertamina sources said.
"The CDU was shut again on Monday because the tanks for residue are full," one source said.
"The CDU has no problem at all. We resumed operations on Friday, Saturday and Sunday, but we shut it again on Monday," the source said.
The source did not say when it would resume operations again.
Pertamina initially shut down the CDU at its Balongan refinery for two days on Wednesday due to technical problems with the residue catalytic cracker (RCC) unit.
The sources said Monday that work on the 83,000-bpd capacity RCC at Balongan was still going on.
The RCC has been closed since February 6 due to an unexpected technical problem and that three weeks were needed for repairs.
Pertamina junior processing director Samto Utomo said on February 25 that attempts to restart the RCC on February 20 had failed because of what he only described as "another small problem."
He did not reveal the exact nature of the problem.
